newsitem.title: ITALY: FIVE ETHIOPIAN SOCCER PLAYERS FLY HOME.
newsitem.headline: FIVE ETHIOPIAN SOCCER PLAYERS FLY HOME.

text.p: Five of the 16 members of Ethiopia's national soccer squad who sought political asylum in Italy, then changed their minds but missed their flight home, finally returned to Addis Ababa, refugee officials said on Saturday.
They said a last minute appeal by the Italian Council for Refugees to persuade the five men to stay on in Italy failed and they boarded a flight on Friday night.
"We didn't manage to convince them," said Mario Lana, a lawyer who helped the Ethiopians with their asylum request. "It was a long shot but we had to give it a try."
The 16 players went missing for more than a day after the 23-member team stopped in Rome on Monday on the way to Casablanca for an African Nations' Cup match against Morocco.
They turned up at the foreigners office of Rome police headquarters and asked for political asylum.

Seven members of the squad did not seek asylum and flew home on Thursday. Mekele Beseka, an official of the Ethiopian team, said the five who changed their mind about asylum had "realised that they had made a mistake".

Lana said he had appealed to the five on behalf of their colleagues staying behind, but to no avail. "They were afraid of reprisals at home for their families, who have surely been put under pressure," he said.
